sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Crestview different from South Florida?
sections.html:
Crestview is an Okaloosa County city, and its owner-occupied homes are valued modestly. Census QuickFacts puts the median value of owner-occupied homes at $277,900 for 2020-2024, against $332,700 for the United States on the same series.

Growth is the local story. The city counted 20,978 people in 2010, 27,134 in the 2020 census, and an estimated 31,193 on July 1, 2025, a 13.8 percent rise from the 2020 estimates base. A median household income of $65,480 shapes what local buyers can pay.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Crestview housing?
sections.html:
Crestview covers 16.58 square miles of land, with about 1,636.8 residents per square mile in 2020, a much lower density than the South Florida cities. Owners occupy 61.3 percent of housing units.

sections.h2: Who lives in Crestview and where do they work?
sections.html:
The population is young. Census lists 28.3 percent under 18 and 11.2 percent 65 or older, and 8.0 percent under 5.

  • 57.4 percent of residents 16 and older are in the civilian labor force.
  • The mean commute is 30.4 minutes, longer than the 26.4 minute national figure.
  • Census counts 2022 retail sales of $931,900 thousand and health care and social assistance receipts of $308,563 thousand.

Bachelor's degree attainment is 22.6 percent, and 92.1 percent of adults 25 and older hold a high school diploma or higher.

sections.h2: Which Okaloosa County offices handle a Crestview sale?
sections.html:
Property records and values sit with the Okaloosa County property appraiser, bills come from the county tax collector, and deeds are recorded by the Okaloosa clerk of the circuit court. Florida gives every county the same five elected offices: sheriff, tax collector, property appraiser, supervisor of elections and clerk.

The appraiser values property each January 1 and decides exemption eligibility. The tax collector mails bills in November, takes deferral and installment applications, and sells tax certificates. The clerk collects documentary stamp tax at recording. Ask each office directly for forms, hours and current fees for your parcel.

sections.h2: What taxes apply when a Crestview home is sold?
sections.html:
Okaloosa County uses the statewide deed rate of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, per the Department of Revenue, and the base rate appears in s. 201.02. Every party on the document is liable no matter which side agrees to pay.

  • Recording at the clerk costs $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, before trust fund and technology charges.
  • A fourth or later name on an instrument adds $1.00 each.
  • The deed needs two witnesses.

A quitclaim deed is taxable as well, and a transfer between spouses may qualify for an exemption when the only consideration is a mortgage on the homestead.

sections.h2: How do homestead rules affect Crestview sellers and buyers?
sections.html:
A Crestview homeowner with a homestead exemption pays tax on a value reduced by up to $50,000, and the first $25,000 applies to school taxes too. The exemption ends when the house is sold, rented out, or no longer your permanent home.

Save Our Homes limits yearly increases to the lower of 3 percent or CPI. In a fast-growing city like Crestview, values can run ahead of that cap, so the buyer's first bill after a sale can jump. Non-homestead property has a separate 10 percent annual limit. A sale, foreclosure or transfer of title counts as a change of ownership and resets the property to just value the next January 1.

sections.h2: What if a Crestview house is tenant-occupied, inherited or behind on payments?
sections.html:
Each case has fixed Florida steps worth knowing before you set a closing date.

  • Tenants: three days for nonpayment, seven days to cure or vacate for lease violations, and 30 days' notice to end a month-to-month tenancy.
  • Estates: summary administration for non-exempt estates of $150,000 or less, and a creditor claim period of three months after first publication of notice.
  • Foreclosure: a sale 20 to 35 days after judgment, a 5 percent bid deposit, and 10 days to object.

Unauthorized occupants are different from tenants. The owner may file a sworn complaint with the sheriff to have them removed, but false statements expose the owner to damages equal to triple the fair market rent.

sections.h2: What does the Florida tax calendar look like for a Crestview owner?
sections.html:
The tax year follows a fixed yearly pattern that applies in Okaloosa County as it does everywhere in Florida.

  • January 1: the assessment date.
  • March 1: filing deadline for exemptions and classifications.
  • August: the property appraiser mails the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes.
  • Within 25 days of that notice: the window to file a value petition with the clerk.
  • November: bills go out, with a 4 percent discount for paying that month, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February.
  • April 1: unpaid taxes become delinquent.

If you are selling near the end of a year, ask your closing agent how the bill is split, because the tax for the whole year arrives after most sales close.

sections.h2: What happens if Crestview property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The tax collector sells a certificate on each unpaid account by June 1, awarding it to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest rate in quarter-percent steps. A certificate holder cannot contact the owner to demand payment until two years after April 1 of the year of issuance, and may apply for a tax deed after that period with a $75 application fee.

On homestead property the opening bid at a tax deed sale includes one-half of the latest assessed value on top of the amounts due. The high bidder at the clerk's auction pays a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater. Selling the house and paying the taxes at closing ends the problem sooner than waiting for an auction.

sections.h2: Can a Crestview owner use a life estate deed or transfer to family?
sections.html:
Florida treats a transfer of title as a change of ownership for assessment unless an exception applies, such as a transfer between spouses. A quitclaim deed and a contract for deed are both taxable documents under the Department of Revenue list.

A so-called lady bird deed was addressed in a 2020 Department of Revenue advisement, which said that the deed on the facts presented transfers no present beneficial interest and so carries no doc stamp tax. That advisement turned on its facts, so have a Florida attorney review any such deed before relying on it.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Crestview?
faqs.a: Census QuickFacts lists $277,900 for owner-occupied housing units in Crestview for 2020-2024.
Census estimates 31,193 residents in July 2025, up 13.8 percent from the April 2020 estimates base.

faqs.q: Do I pay documentary stamp tax when I sell in Crestview?
faqs.a: The deed is taxable at 70 cents per $100 in Okaloosa County, and every party to it is liable. Who actually pays is a matter of the sales contract.

faqs.q: Who can tell me my current property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Okaloosa County tax collector sends the bill each November, and the property appraiser can explain the value and exemptions behind it.

faqs.q: Can an heir sell a house before probate ends?
faqs.a: Usually not until the personal representative has authority. Ask a probate lawyer or the clerk about the right track, such as summary administration for smaller estates.
